note: Registration Role has exactly one config object, registration_role.setting (SINGULAR 'setting'), with keys role_to_select (sequence of role ids) and registration_mode ('user' = self registration only, 'admin' = also when another user or a CLI script creates the account). Form route registration_role.setting.form at /admin/people/registration-role, gated by its own permission 'administer registration roles'. All runtime behaviour is registration_role_user_presave(): roles are added only when $user->isNew() and either the current user is anonymous and PHP_SAPI is not cli, or registration_mode is 'admin'. That CLI detail is what makes the hard cases verifiable: a Drush-created user gets the roles only in 'admin' mode. No tables, no services, no plugins, no Drush commands.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal 11 site with the registration_role module, which configuration object stores which roles are auto-assigned to new users, what are its keys, and what is the admin path of its settings form?
evals.expected_output: The config object is registration_role.setting (singular 'setting', not 'settings'), with keys role_to_select (a sequence of role ids) and registration_mode ('user' or 'admin'). The form is at /admin/people/registration-role, route registration_role.setting.form, permission 'administer registration roles'.

evals.prompt: The Drupal registration_role module has a 'Registration mode' setting. What are the two possible values, what does each one mean, and does a user account created by a Drush script get the configured roles?
evals.expected_output: registration_mode is either 'user' (User self registration - roles only when an anonymous visitor registers) or 'admin' (Both user self registration and user creation by admin). registration_role_user_presave() treats PHP_SAPI === 'cli' like an admin-created account, so a Drush-created user receives the roles only when registration_mode is 'admin'.

evals.prompt: In the Drupal registration_role module, which hook actually assigns the roles, and will editing an existing user account re-apply the configured roles?
evals.expected_output: registration_role_user_presave(), an implementation of hook_ENTITY_TYPE_presave() for user entities. It only calls $user->addRole() when $user->isNew() is TRUE, so saving or editing an existing account never re-applies the roles, and a manually removed role is not restored.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has the registration_role module configured. Inspect the live configuration and tell me which role is automatically given to new users, and whether accounts created by an administrator also receive it.
evals.expected_output: registration_role.setting:role_to_select contains registration_role_known and registration_mode is 'admin', so administrator-created (and CLI-created) accounts get it too. Read it with: drush cget registration_role.setting

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, registration_role hands out some roles when people sign up. Inspect the running site: how many roles are given out, which ones, and does an account created by an administrator on the People screen get them?
evals.expected_output: Two roles: registration_role_alpha and registration_role_beta. registration_mode is 'user' (self registration only), so accounts an administrator creates do NOT get them. Read it with: drush cget registration_role.setting

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has the registration_role module enabled and a role with machine name registration_role_task. Configure the live site so every newly created user account gets that role - not only people who register themselves, but also accounts created by an administrator or by a script. Apply the configuration to the running site.
evals.expected_output: Set registration_role.setting:role_to_select to include registration_role_task and registration_role.setting:registration_mode to 'admin' (Both user self registration and user creation by admin). The verify script then creates a user from the CLI and requires that it really comes out with the role.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a role called 'Registration Role Self Only' (machine name registration_role_selfonly). People who sign up for an account themselves should get that role automatically - but accounts that our staff create for someone must NOT get it. That role should be the only one handed out on registration. Set this up on the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set registration_role.setting:role_to_select to exactly [registration_role_selfonly] and registration_role.setting:registration_mode to 'user' (User self registration). The verify script creates an account from the CLI -- which registration_role treats as admin-created -- and requires that it does NOT receive the role.
